description: A data-engineering session on Project Helios that drifts across three topics (Airflow ETL design, Grafana dashboards, cloud cost optimization) before returning to the original pipeline task. Stresses intent persistence across topic drift and all-user-message compression (segments 1, 2, 6, 8).

transcript.content: I'm setting up the ETL pipeline for Project Helios. We need to ingest daily CRM exports into the warehouse. Can you help me design the Airflow DAG?
Sure. For CRM exports I'd recommend a three-task DAG: extract, validate, load, with a data-quality gate between validate and load. What's the source system and where do the files land?
The source is Salesforce, exporting about 2GB of CSVs daily to the S3 bucket s3://helios-crm-exports. The warehouse is Snowflake.

Salesforce to S3 to Snowflake is a solid pattern. I'd use an external Snowflake stage on the S3 bucket and COPY INTO with match_by_column_name. For validation, run row-count and schema checks before load. One decision to make: full vs incremental load.
Incremental. We only get deltas after the first backfill. Let's use an updated_at watermark column.
Good choice. Watermark column updated_at, incremental loads, and we'll track the high-water mark in a control table etl_ctl.load_watermarks. What schedule should the DAG run on?
Daily at 3am UTC, after the Salesforce export finishes at 2:30am UTC.

Daily at 3am UTC it is, cron '0 3 * * *'. I'll add a sensor on the S3 prefix with a 30-minute timeout as a safety net so a late export doesn't cause a partial load. That completes the pipeline design. Anything else?
Switching topics. Leadership wants a Grafana dashboard for pipeline health. What should we track?

For pipeline health I'd track four golden signals: DAG success rate over 7 days, average task duration per task, rows loaded per run versus the 7-day median, and data-freshness lag, meaning now minus max(updated_at) in the warehouse. Alert on freshness over 26 hours and success rate under 95 percent.
Good. Which Grafana datasource should we use for Snowflake?

The Grafana Snowflake datasource plugin works fine over a warehouse read-only role. Create a dedicated grafana_ro role with usage on the ETL schema only. Don't reuse the loader role, or a dashboard misconfiguration could write to your load tables.
Makes sense. The dashboard name should be 'Helios Pipeline Health' and I'll put it in the 'Data Platform' folder.

Noted: dashboard 'Helios Pipeline Health' in folder 'Data Platform', datasource Snowflake via grafana_ro. Four panels: success rate, task duration, rows loaded, freshness lag. Anything else for the dashboard?
That's the dashboard settled. Now costs. The Snowflake bill jumped 40 percent last month. Where do we start?

A 40 percent jump usually traces to one of three things: warehouse auto-suspend disabled, runaway queries from ad-hoc BI, or credit-burning clone testing. Start with the QUERY_HISTORY audit grouped by warehouse, ordered by credits. Also check whether the ETL warehouse has auto-suspend at 60 seconds.
I checked. Our ETL warehouse XS had auto-suspend disabled. I've enabled it with a 60-second auto-suspend.

That alone typically recovers 15 to 25 percent of ETL spend. Next, isolate non-critical workloads like the backfill from interactive traffic. Snowflake doesn't have spot instances, but multi-cluster warehouses let you separate batch from interactive.
What about the Airflow workers themselves? We're on EC2 and the bill there is up too.

For Airflow workers on EC2 the equivalent of spot savings is literally Spot Instances: run the workers on Spot with a fallback to on-demand via an ASG mixed-instances policy. Schedule-tolerant ETL is the textbook Spot workload. Set max price at 70 percent of on-demand.
Okay, I'll migrate the Airflow workers to Spot with a 70 percent max price and a mixed ASG. Coming back to the main thread now: what's left to ship the Helios pipeline?

Remaining for the pipeline: one, the backfill DAG for the first full load; two, the watermark control table migration; three, alerting on freshness wired to PagerDuty; four, a runbook for reruns. The design itself (incremental on updated_at, daily 3am UTC, S3 sensor) is complete.
Who else is on the team? I want to assign the runbook.
You've mentioned you're the data engineer; for a runbook you'd typically loop in the on-call SRE. I don't have the team roster. Who else is on Helios?
It's me, Marta, data engineer, and Daniel from SRE. Daniel will take the runbook and the PagerDuty rotation.
Team noted: Marta (data engineer) on the pipeline, Daniel (SRE) on the runbook and PagerDuty rotation. Ownership is settled. Deadline-wise you haven't stated one. Is there a target date?
We need the pipeline live by March 15th for the quarterly board review.

March 15th for go-live, ahead of the quarterly board review, roughly three weeks out. Given the design is complete, the critical path is backfill duration. I'd dry-run the full load this week to size it.
One more decision: the Snowflake warehouse size for the ETL loads, XS or S?

Start XS for daily deltas; 2GB of CSV should load in minutes. Size S only if the backfill would run over the weekend window. Keep auto-suspend at 60 seconds as you configured, so it stays consistent with the cost work.
Fine, XS for daily and S for the backfill window. I think we've covered everything. Summarize the decisions?

Decisions: incremental load on the updated_at watermark into Snowflake via an external stage on s3://helios-crm-exports; daily 3am UTC with an S3 sensor and 30-minute timeout; Grafana 'Helios Pipeline Health' in 'Data Platform' with grafana_ro; EC2 cost fix via 60-second auto-suspend plus Spot workers at 70 percent max price; team Marta and Daniel; go-live March 15th; warehouse XS daily and S for backfill.
Perfect. Last thing: the CRM team asked whether we can also ingest their marketing events later. Should we design for that now?

Design for it cheaply: keep the DAG generic per source and add future sources as new DAGs rather than one monolith. Marketing events can be a second DAG later, since events are append-only with no watermark complexity. Don't build it now; that's YAGNI until the CRM pipeline is live.

facts.text: The ETL pipeline ingests daily Salesforce CRM CSV exports (about 2GB/day) from S3 bucket s3://helios-crm-exports into Snowflake.
Loads are incremental using an updated_at watermark column, with the high-water mark tracked in control table etl_ctl.load_watermarks.
The DAG is scheduled daily at 3am UTC, after the Salesforce export finishes at 2:30am UTC.
An S3 prefix sensor with a 30-minute timeout guards against late exports.
The Grafana dashboard 'Helios Pipeline Health' lives in folder 'Data Platform' and tracks DAG success rate, task duration, rows loaded, and freshness lag.
Grafana reads Snowflake through a dedicated read-only grafana_ro role with usage on the ETL schema only.
Alert thresholds: data freshness over 26 hours; DAG success rate under 95 percent.
The Snowflake bill jumped 40 percent last month, traced to auto-suspend being disabled on the ETL XS warehouse; it is now enabled with a 60-second auto-suspend.
Airflow EC2 workers migrate to Spot Instances with max price 70 percent of on-demand, via a mixed-instances ASG with on-demand fallback.
Team: Marta (data engineer) owns the pipeline; Daniel (SRE) owns the runbook and the PagerDuty rotation.
Pipeline go-live deadline is March 15th, ahead of the quarterly board review.
Warehouse sizing: XS for daily deltas, S for the backfill window.
Remaining pipeline work: backfill DAG, watermark control-table migration, PagerDuty freshness alerting, rerun runbook.
Marketing-events ingestion is deferred (YAGNI); future sources will be added as separate DAGs, not one monolith.
